ideas.name: FocalShift
ideas.niche: AI-driven aspect ratio conversion and intelligent re-framing for social media optimization.
ideas.problem: The tedious, manual process of keyframing landscape (16:9) footage into vertical (9:16) formats, which often results in lost subjects, awkward compositions, and massive time loss for creators.
ideas.targetUser: Independent video creators, social media managers, and YouTube editors (ages 18-35) who need to rapidly repurpose long-form content into high-engagement vertical clips for TikTok, Reels, and Shorts.
coreFeatures: AI Subject-Lock Tracking: Automatically detects and maintains focus on the primary human or object subject through movement.
Compositional Weight Analysis: Uses Rule of Thirds and Golden Ratio algorithms to intelligently center elements based on visual importance rather than just geometry.
Batch Sequence Reframing: Applies consistent reframing logic across entire video timelines or multiple clips simultaneously.
Predictive Smooth-Pan: Generates non-jittery, cinematic camera pans by interpolating movement between detected subject positions.
realDependencies: Computer Vision Engine (TensorFlow or OpenCV) for real-time object detection and segmentation
FFmpeg or Cloud-based GPU Rendering Engine for high-speed video transcoding
Cloud Storage API (AWS S3 or Google Cloud Storage) for managing large video assets
Machine Learning Inference API for compositional analysis
ideas.emulationStrategy: To simulate the high-compute experience, the app will use a local library of pre-selected MP4 files. When a user 'processes' a video, a simulated loading state will trigger a progress bar that increments at variable, non-linear speeds using `setInterval` to mimic heavy CPU/GPU usage. The AI 'detection' will be faked by mapping specific timecodes in the mock videos to a hardcoded JSON object containing pre-calculated 'bounding box' coordinates. Instead of actual video rendering, the UI will use CSS `transform: scale()` and `object-position` properties on the HTML5 video element to visually jump and slide the view to the 'newly framed' coordinates, creating a convincing illusion of real-time re-framing.

ideas.name: AuraSonic
ideas.problem: Traditional metadata relies on literal object descriptions (e.g., 'metal hit', 'bird chirp'), making it impossible for sound designers to search for the emotional intent or textural 'vibe' (e.g., 'menacing', 'ethereal', 'brittle') required for high-level cinematic scoring and sound design.
ideas.targetUser: Professional sound designers, foley artists, and game audio engineers in AAA film and gaming studios who manage massive (1TB+) unorganized libraries and work under tight deadlines to match specific scene moods.
coreFeatures: Affective Semantic Search: A natural language interface allowing users to search for emotions (e.g., 'increasing dread') rather than objects.
Spectral Vibe Mapping: A 2D/3D visual navigation space where assets are plotted based on psychoacoustic dimensions like 'Brightness vs. Darkness' and 'Weight vs. Airiness'.
Neural Texture Tagging: An automated background engine that analyzes audio waveforms to assign psychoacoustic descriptors via deep learning.
Emotional Palette Generation: A feature that analyzes a music track or video clip to suggest a cohesive set of SFX textures that match the existing mood.
realDependencies: TensorFlow or PyTorch for deep learning-based audio feature extraction
Pinecone or Milvus for high-dimensional vector similarity search
Librosa or Essentia for spectral and temporal signal processing
AWS S3 or similar object storage for massive-scale asset hosting
ideas.emulationStrategy: The demo will use a local JSON 'Master Manifest' containing 50 pre-defined mock assets, each with a set of 'Vibe Coefficients' (e.g., {dread: 0.8, shimmer: 0.1, weight: 0.9}). To simulate AI-heavy processing, any search or tagging action will trigger a 2.5-second asynchronous delay accompanied by a 'Neural Feature Extraction' progress bar. The search engine will not use real NLP; instead, it will use a keyword-to-coefficient mapping function (e.g., typing 'scary' triggers a search for assets where 'dread' > 0.7) to return results from the mock manifest, creating a convincing illusion of semantic understanding.

ideas.name: KineticCue
ideas.niche: Frame-accurate motion graphics feedback and review
ideas.problem: The 'Vague Feedback Loop' where clients use non-technical language (e.g., 'make it snappier') without providing specific timecodes or visual context for easing and timing changes.
ideas.targetUser: Freelance motion designers and boutique animation studios (ages 22-40) who struggle to translate client 'feelings' into technical interpolation adjustments.
coreFeatures: Frame-Locked Annotation: Pin comments to specific frames rather than just timestamps to prevent drift.
Ease-Curve Sketching: A simplified UI allowing clients to draw a rough 'S-curve' to describe desired acceleration/deceleration.
Ghosting Comparison: Overlay a previous version's movement as a semi-transparent layer over the current version to visualize timing shifts.
Zero-Friction Client Link: A lightweight, browser-based view that requires no login or software installation for the client.
realDependencies: Mux or Cloudinary for high-bitrate video streaming and frame-accurate seeking
FFmpeg for server-side frame extraction and preview generation
Firebase Realtime Database for instant multi-user annotation syncing
AWS S3 for heavy motion graphic file storage
ideas.emulationStrategy: The demo will use a local MP4 file and a hardcoded JSON object containing a set of 'mock_comments' mapped to specific 'frame_id' integers. To simulate real-world latency, all 'Save Comment' and 'Upload' actions will be wrapped in a 1.5-second setTimeout with a UI loading spinner. Video 'processing' will be faked by a 4-second CSS progress bar that triggers a 'Processing Complete' state, revealing the hardcoded JSON comments once the bar reaches 100%.

ideas.name: ZoneCheck
ideas.niche: Social media composition and UI occlusion validation
ideas.problem: High-production value content is frequently ruined when platform-specific interactive elements (like TikTok's comment sidebar or Instagram's caption area) cover essential visual information, text, or faces.
ideas.targetUser: Social media managers, short-form video editors, motion designers, and digital ad agencies producing high-volume mobile-first content.
coreFeatures: Multi-platform UI mask library (TikTok, IG Reels, YouTube Shorts, FB Stories)
Real-time drag-and-drop asset previewing
Dynamic opacity toggling for platform overlay layers
Safe-zone heatmap visualization to identify 'dead zones' for text and logos
realDependencies: AWS S3 for high-resolution video/image storage
Cloudinary or FFmpeg for real-time client-side video rendering
RESTful API for periodic UI asset updates (as platforms change layouts)
Firebase Authentication for user workspace management
ideas.emulationStrategy: The demo will use a local directory of sample .mp4 and .png files to simulate S3 assets. A 'Processing' state will be triggered by a 2-second randomized timeout to mimic cloud rendering. All platform UI overlays will be stored as static SVG layers within the frontend state rather than being fetched from an external library. API calls will be intercepted via a mock service layer that returns pre-defined JSON objects with a simulated 500ms latency to mimic real network conditions.

ideas.name: VibeScale
ideas.problem: The 'Translation Gap' where subjective marketing adjectives (e.g., 'moody,' 'high-octane,' 'premium') lead to mismatched creative outputs, resulting in costly revisions and friction between brand managers and technical creators.
ideas.targetUser: Freelance motion designers, video editors, and sound engineers (ages 22-40) working on remote contracts, and Creative Directors at mid-sized agencies needing to standardize briefing processes.
coreFeatures: Semantic Sentiment Parser: An NLP-driven text field that extracts stylistic intent from unstructured brand briefs.
Technical Parameter Blueprint: Generates specific values for BPM, Color Temperature (K), Shutter Angle, LUT suggestions, and Motion Curves.
Reference Engine: Maps aesthetic keywords to specific YouTube/Spotify metadata to provide auditory and visual benchmarks.
Standardized Handover Export: Creates a 'Technical Manifesto' in PDF or JSON format to be attached to project contracts or briefs.
realDependencies: OpenAI GPT-4o API (for semantic mapping and linguistic nuance)
Pinecone Vector Database (to store and retrieve mappings of adjectives to technical ranges)
YouTube Data API (to find visual reference matches)
Spotify Web API (to analyze audio characteristics like energy and tempo for sound design specs)
ideas.emulationStrategy: The demo will use a local JSON dictionary that maps 50 common marketing adjectives (e.g., 'Luxury', 'Gritty', 'Pop') to pre-defined technical value ranges. All 'API calls' will be handled by a local service layer that uses `setTimeout` to simulate a 2.5-second 'Thinking...' state. Mock media references will be pulled from a hardcoded array of YouTube IDs and Spotify tracks rather than live fetching, ensuring a fast, reliable, and consistent demo experience.
